changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments-led buyers (a head of payments or similar): "Here are your approvals by market, by card type and issuer, the money you're leaving on the table in each one, and what we'll fix." Use 'approvals', not 'authorization'. Name Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance second, as the how. Keep the average uplift only as a footnote. Once product confirms our coverage, add one line per market on how we handle local cards (his phrase: 'local cards, local rails').
changes.why: He rejected the M4 average outright ('that's an average. What's mine?', 'I can't take an average to my CFO'), says 'approvals' and 'money left on the table', and after Adyen's test he framed his questions by country, card type, issuer and why.

changes.change: When a competitor offers a traffic test: "Your approval analysis by market, on your own existing traffic, in days, not weeks. Each country comes with the cause (issuer, card type, local vs cross-border) and the fixes." Use this only after the payments performance team commits to that turnaround as an operating standard.
changes.why: Adyen won with country-level results on his own traffic. Our tailored analysis, with fixable findings, was the most useful thing we sent him, but it arrived three weeks after he asked and after their test had finished.

changes.change: Proof point to sit next to M5 support tiers, for accounts of this kind: "A named payments performance contact who reviews your approvals by market with you every month." Publish it only once that coverage actually exists.
changes.why: He asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, and he said he only heard from Stripe when he said he was leaving. M5's response times answer a different question.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For accounts that have just hired a payments owner: don't open with the global-growth line. Open with "Your approvals by country, and where you're losing revenue," offered as a proactive review in their first weeks.
changes.why: The original buyer left, and the new head of payments' first move was to pull declines by country, so a generic global-growth opener misses what this buyer judges us on from day one.
